texts.preamble: Prabhakar Singh (Dar) vs Anil Kwatra (88/20 Bp) on 8 December, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No.863/24 Prabhakar Singh vs. Anil Kwatra & ors. Cnr No.DLSE01-009988-2022 1. Prabhakar Singh S/o Sh. Tej Singh R/o H. No.A-253, Meethapur Part-2, New Delhi-110044 ....Claimant/Petitioner Versus 1. Anil Kwatra S/o Sh. Subhash Chandra Kwatra R/o House no.40, Ram Nagar, Distt. Karnal, Haryana ....Driver /Respondent no.1 2. Ganga Pal S/o Sh. Radhacharan R/o House no.F-156, Shahbad Diary, Delhi 110042. ....Owner/Respondent no.2 Mact no.863/2024 Prabhakar Singh vs. Anil Kwatra & ors. Page no. 1 of 21 ss Digitally signed by Charu Charu Gupta Gupta Date: 2025.12.08 16:53:09 +0530 3. Shri Ram General Insurance Company Ltd. Office at: 1001, Gf, Arya Samaj Road, Naiwala, Karol Bagh, New Delhi-110005 ....Insurance company/Respondent no.3 Date of accident : 17.03.2020 Result of accident : Grievous injury Date of filing of Dar : 18.10.2022 Date of Decision : 08.12.2025 Award 1. The present Detailed Accident Report arises out of road accident that occurred on 17.03.2020, in which one Prabhakar Singh (aged about 36 years) allegedly suffered grievous injury.
texts.facts: Brief facts of the case are that on 17.03.2020 Prabhakar Singh was traveling from Gautam Nagar to Badarpur on motorcycle. When he reached the red light at Ali Road before Badarpur Flyover, a vehicle (Taxi) no. DL-1ZC-1603 (hereinafter referred to the offending vehicle) came at a very high speed, driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the victim. Due to this victim fell and sustained injuries. He was removed to AIIMS Trauma Center. 3. An FIR no.88/2020, dated 18.03.2020 was registered u/s 279/337 IPC at PS Badarpur, District South-East. Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet u/s 279/338 of IPC before concerned criminal court while DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by MACT no.863/2024 Prabhakar Singh vs. Anil Kwatra & ors. Page no. 2 of 21 ss Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.12.08 16:53:13 +0530 respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3. 5. Respondent no.1 and 2 did not file their reply despite opportunity. 6. Written statement /reply was filed by respondent no.3 refuting its liability to compensate the petitioners pleading that respondent no.2 was in breach of the terms of the insurance policy in as much as respondent no.1 was not holding a valid driving licence on the date of accident. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 05.11.2024. OPP 2. OPP. 3. Relief. 8. In order to prove his claim, petitioner examined himself as PW-1. To prove his claim, petitioner /Prabhakar Singh led evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He deposed that on 17.03.2020 he was going on his motorcycle towards Badarpur from Gautam Nagar. One vehicle/Taxi bearing no. DL-1ZC-1603 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit his motorcycle at Ali Road Red Light before Badarpur Flyover. Petitioner fell on the road. Due to the collusion, driver of offending vehicle took the injured to AIIMS Trauma Center and left. Page no. 3 of 21 ss Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.12.08 16:53:16 +0530 AIIMS Trauma Center. Prabhakar Singh (Dar) vs Anil Kwatra (88/20 Bp) on 8 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49256805/ 2 PW1 remained admitted in hospital for 5 days w.e.f. 18.03.2020 to 22.03.2020. He deposed that he underwent surgery and a rod was implanted in his elbow. He further deposed that he was working at Rahul Medicos, Gautam Nagar, New Delhi as a Sales Executive and earning of Rs.25,000/- per month. PW-1 relied upon DAR as Ex.PW1/1, MLC marked as Mark A, discharge summary as Ex.PW1/3, Office ID as Ex.PW1/4, medical bills/documents as Ex.PW1/5, Adhar card as Ex.PW1/6 and driving licence as Ex.PW1/7. PW-1 was duly cross examined by insurance company. 9. Respondent no.3/insurance company led its evidence by examining Prasoon Kumar, Senior Executive Legal, Shriram General Insurance Company Limited. R3W1 tendered his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.R3W1/A. He deposed that respondent no.1 had taken policy no.10003/31/20/293711 for his vehicle bearing no.DL-1ZC-1603 for period 20.09.2019 to 19.09.2020. He deposed that the driver was not holding a valid driving licence at the time of accident. He further deposed that insurance company sent its investigator to verify the driving licence of respondent no.1 from RTO Karnal. The dealing clerk of RTO verbally informed to investigator that the DL's record was not available in the RTO office records. The investigator even filed an RTI application to know the status of driving licence. No reply to that application was received. Date: 2025.12.08 16:53:20 +0530 report as Ex.R3W1/3 and RTI application as Ex.R3W1/4. He was cross examined by Ld. Counsel for petitioner. Respondent no.1 and 2 did not lead any evidence despite opportunity. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents. Petitioner has claimed to be working as a sales executive at Rahul Medicos and earning approximate Rs.25,000/- per month. As already discussed, principal award amount/ compensation will be payable by respondents with simple interest @7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till actual realization. Insurance company is hereby directed to deposit the award amount in favour of the petitioner with State Bank of India, District Court Complex, Saket Court Branch, New Delhi by way of RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in account of MACT SAVING ACCOUNT, A/c No.00000042706875094, IFS Code SBIN0014244 and MICR code 110002342 under intimation to the Nazir along with calculation of interest and to the Counsel for the petitioner.
texts.arguments: (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 14. It may further be noted that in Cholamandalam Insurance Company vs. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 17. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011)1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. 18.6. It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a). 18.7. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench MACT no.863/2024 Prabhakar Singh vs. Anil Kwatra & ors. However, in a recent judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India titled as Parminder Singh vs Honey Goyal on 18 March, 2025 in S.L.P. (C) No. 4484 OF 2020 has held that : "17. 29.
